instruction:
Use NASA's Mercury facts page to distinguish a year, an axial rotation and a solar day on Mercury. Report each duration in Earth days using the page's rounded values. Identify which duration measures a complete day-night cycle and calculate how many Mercury years fit in that cycle. Give the relevant section heading and source URL; keep the three kinds of period separate.

Stopping condition: Stop when the three labelled durations, the day-night identification and the year-to-solar-day ratio are supported by the NASA page.

Constraints:
- Only use the browser actions available to you. Do not open API endpoints, raw data files, view-source pages or downloads, and do not use external programs.
- Do not sign in or create accounts. Do not provide anyone's private personal information; use only task-supplied fictional values if an interaction requests personal details.
- Remain read-only: do not purchase, reserve, apply, post, send messages, contact people or change external records.
- Navigation, search, filtering, sorting and read-only form or calculator interactions are allowed.
- Do not bypass authentication, paywalls, CAPTCHAs or access challenges. Dismiss optional prompts without creating an account or supplying personal information.
- Support the answer with observed page evidence and source URLs. For values that can change, report what the site shows during the run. Preserve the requested dates, units and scope; report unavailable information explicitly instead of inventing it.

items.criterion: Access and Report the Source URL
items.description: Report the source URL used to gather the facts. Full credit if the agent includes the NASA Mercury facts URL (e.g., https://science.nasa.gov/mercury/facts/) in its output. Full credit if the page is down/inaccessible and the agent reports this.

Provide the relevant section heading from the NASA page where the time/rotation information is located. Full credit if the accurate heading (e.g., 'Time on Mercury') is reported, if the page structure has changed and the agent accurately reports the current relevant heading, OR if the page is inaccessible/the info is missing and the agent reports this.

Report the duration of a year on Mercury in Earth days. Full credit if the agent reports 88 Earth days (or the rounded value currently present on the page), OR if the page is inaccessible/the info is missing and the agent reports this. Partial credit if the agent reports an unrounded value when the rounded value was requested and available.

Report the duration of an axial rotation on Mercury in Earth days. Full credit if the agent reports 59 Earth days (or the rounded value currently present on the page), OR if the page is inaccessible/the info is missing and the agent reports this. Partial credit if the agent reports an unrounded value when the rounded value was requested and available.

Report the duration of a solar day on Mercury in Earth days. Full credit if the agent reports 176 Earth days (or the rounded value currently present on the page), OR if the page is inaccessible/the info is missing and the agent reports this. Partial credit if the agent reports an unrounded value when the rounded value was requested and available.

Keep the three kinds of period (year, axial rotation, and solar day) separate in the final output as requested. Full credit if they are clearly distinguished and not conflated, OR if the page was inaccessible/the info missing and the agent correctly reported this limitation without conflating information.

Identify which of the three durations measures a complete day-night cycle on Mercury. Full credit if the agent correctly identifies the Solar Day (176 Earth days) as the complete day-night cycle based on the text, OR if the page is inaccessible/the info is missing and the agent reports this.

items.criterion: Calculate Mercury Years per Day-Night Cycle
items.description: Calculate how many Mercury years fit into that day-night cycle. Full credit if the agent calculates 2 years (176 divided by 88) or accurately computes the ratio based on the specific numbers found on the page during the run, OR if the page is inaccessible/the info is missing and the agent reports this.
